statisticsConvention: All durations include unsuccessful attempts when present. Median uses the middle value or average of the two middle values; p95 is nearest-rank ceil(0.95*n). Missing browser captures remain null.

limitations: Finite bursts, not sustained multi-user load or throughput capacity.

processObservations.installedNextCondition: getMemoryRestartStats triggers the development worker restart when heapUsed exceeds 80% of heapSizeLimit; this is not an OOM event.

postBurstRssSnapshot.limitations: A process RSS snapshot includes native/code/buffer memory. It is neither peak RSS nor JavaScript heapUsed.

processObservations.limitations: Worker replacement happened during the burst. This run contains cold compilation, stalls and failed requests; it cannot be described as uniformly warm or stable.

limitations: Finite bursts, not sustained multi-user load or throughput capacity.

processObservations.rssInterpretation: Start and end snapshots, not peaks or JavaScript heapUsed.
processObservations.limitations: Fresh explicit 8 GiB process, whereas the 4 GiB process was aged. Compiled state, background activity and live data were not held fixed. This finite observation does not establish causality or long-session longevity.

limitations: GET-only finite bursts using the same legitimate authenticated user/session; no business writes, authentication bypass or response bodies recorded.
Each run has 20 requests per route/origin/concurrency combination, 360 total. The groups were sequential, not simultaneous across all routes.
Public HTTP duration includes network/Tunnel overhead and response-body consumption. Server-Timing is a development read scope, not full request compilation or browser latency.
SQL and pool timings sum driver dispatch/acquisition spans and can exceed scope wall time when operations overlap; driver counts include transaction and session-control dispatches.
Neither finite run is a sustained multi-user throughput or long-session reliability test. No request failure, first-hit compilation or slow outlier was excluded.

The same-source 8 GiB run started a fresh worker; the earlier 4 GiB worker had accumulated compilation state. Different session age and compiled state prevent attributing request differences to heap size alone.
concurrency.responseValidation: A success means HTTP 200 and JSON.parse succeeded with a data key and no error key. The helper did not retain bodies or assert completeness, total counts, individual approval sources, live permissions or business parity.

workResponseBytes.limitations: Equal response byte lengths do not prove identical data or complete approval-source coverage.

browser.method: Intentional full document reloads in the existing authenticated Chrome session; CDP DOMContentLoaded plus visible heading/control check
limitations: DOMContentLoaded is not hydration, interaction readiness or Core Web Vitals.
readyUpperMs includes browser automation and RPC/selector overhead; it is an upper bound, not an isolated application latency.
People rounds 2/3 bridge failures lacked metric capture; round17 did not verify the control within three waits. Later page observations verified the role, People status and saved draft.
Role/heading readiness was used for Work and People1–8; People9–20 used the observed CSS select aria-label. Readiness methods are not a controlled comparative benchmark.
Source edits and other browser/service activity occurred during the run; no slow/failed observations were discarded.
Profiler.enable was unavailable through this browser capability; CPU attribution remains unestablished.
People draft remained saved; Work Search returned six matching items; no business record, draft, role or company was changed.
Normal existing authenticated Console session through public development origin.
Full reload and CDP DOMContentLoaded timings; not SPA transitions, INP or isolated hydration.
Control readiness is an observation upper bound including browser bridge round trips.
All bridge errors and failed control checks retained. Missing measurements are not successes.
Concurrent source changes/background activity and differing control probes prevent a causal navigation before/after claim.
PMS settings first ten samples overlapped source/check activity; final ten were taken after checks. Front browser verification omitted per user's API/tests choice.
The edit marker appeared with unchanged NavigationStart and a 13,168ms client Fast Refresh interval. The observation upper bound also includes browser bridge round trips and background activity.
The later restore observation found the marker absent but NavigationStart had changed. No no-reload restore latency is claimed.

componentHotReload.clientEventWindowLimit: Multiple rebuilding/done events occurred; these bracket the earliest rebuild to last done around each marker observation. Individual printed done intervals are not the whole edit latency.
limitations: Single read-only component attribute cycle; observation timings include tool round trips, compiler state and background traffic. Not a controlled bundler or long-session comparison.

peopleInitialJavaScript.method: Parse the People client-reference manifest entryJSFiles for the page and holding layout, union the page entry with route build-manifest rootMainFiles, deduplicate paths, and sum byte sizes. Report polyfillFiles separately. Gzip estimates compress each emitted file independently at level 9 with mtime 0.
limitations: These are production-build entry manifest byte estimates, not measured downloaded bytes, Brotli transfer size, hydration cost or dev compilation cost.

Before and after builds were not taken from a fully frozen common source snapshot; concurrent unrelated changes existed. The optional panel edit scope does not establish that every byte change was caused by those imports.
The final heap-default build has byte-identical application src to the after-import snapshot, as independently reported by the build agent; its launcher fallback differs.
The initial entry union excludes lazy loadable chunks until requested. A raw webpack development route chunk is a different measurement.

sanitization: Includes route labels and allowlisted paged/view selection values only. Excludes cookies, credentials, personal data, response bodies, SQL text/parameters, request correlation UUIDs and component marker strings.

developmentChoice.reason: The aged 4 GiB development worker reached Next’s automatic used-heap restart threshold during the finite burst. The explicit fresh 8 GiB run and subsequent component HMR completed with the listener unchanged and no automatic memory restart log events. The selected budget provides headroom; it is not an established latency improvement or sustained heap-retention solution.
developmentChoice.overridePolicy: Explicit 4 GiB/8 GiB selection and caller NODE_OPTIONS remain supported.
remainingLimitations: Finite GET bursts and a single component edit/restore do not establish long-session reliability.
Heap retention and sustained memory behavior still require investigation.
No claim that webpack/8 GiB is the fastest variant.
